body.statement: In fine-parameter space, failure of the odd-factor graph recursion is contained in \(\bigcup_{j\to i\in G}\{A_{ii}=A_{jj}=0\}\). For any fixed even diagonal-root branch, failure is contained in \(\bigcup_{j\to i\in G}\{A_{ii}=-A_{jj}\}\). Outside these proper algebraic sets, each diagonal branch produces at most one recursively determined \(A\) and at most one diagonal \(D\), after which the full \((B,Q)\) equations only filter branches.
body.justification: The theorem promotes isolated examples to an algebraically generic identification-and-ambiguity phase diagram.
body.gap: No cited subsampling paper identifies the exact graph-indexed exceptional varieties for target recovery.
body.consumer: It supports diagnostics that route almost every compatible odd-factor input through a closed form and reserve CAD for named collision strata.
